question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}+3x.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
{f}^{'}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+3x)=2x+3
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(-1,-2):$

$$
m={f}^{'}(-1)=2(-1)+3=-2+3=1
$$

Therefore, the slope ${m}^{'}$ of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}^{'} & =-\frac{1}{m} \\  & =-\frac{1}{1} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)=x^{2} + 6 x.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x^{2} + 6 x)=2 x + 6
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,7):$

$$
m=f'(1)=2\cdot (1)+6=2+6=8
$$

Therefore, the slope $m'$ of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m' & =-\frac{1}{m} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(8)} \\  & =- \frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
